extracted.intended_audience: Navy and DoD acquisition and operations personnel, MSC managers, policy analysts, and researchers studying OMB Circular A-76 implementation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for applying OMB Circular A-76 to MSC Nucleus Fleet Special Mission ship operations, including cost-comparison procedures, statement-of-work and quality-assurance requirements, and decision/appeal processes. Focuses on how to prepare, evaluate, and administer in-house vs. contract performance for ship service functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: Efficiency and least cost
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of Circular A-76 is to provide the most efficient operation at the least cost to government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions to perform functions in-house or by contract should be driven by which option yields the most efficient operation at the least government cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five exceptions allowing in-house performance
rubrics_metrics.description: When in-house performance is permissible even if commercial sources exist: (1) Procurement from commercial sources would disrupt or delay a DOD program; (2) In-house performance is necessary to maintain military training or readiness; (3) A satisfactory commercial source is not available; (4) Products or services are available from other federal agencies; (5) Contract performance is more costly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These exceptions determine eligibility for exclusion from A-76 commercial sourcing; they must be considered before initiating cost comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently governmental functions exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Profit-seeking firms are not appropriate sources for services that are 'inherently governmental in nature' (examples: judicial functions, law enforcement, conduct of foreign policy, national defense, intelligence and counter-intelligence operations, tax collection, regulation of industry and commerce, financial administration of government).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such functions are excluded from the A-76 policy and must remain government-performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventory requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB Circular A-76 requires all executive agencies to develop an inventory of their activities and determine which should remain government functions versus those suitable for commercial performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must maintain and annually update this inventory; DOD maintains its list centrally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-step A-76 application procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A-76 application follows: (1) identify activities appropriate for commercial performance; (2) examine each site for special circumstances that might preclude commercial sources; (3) perform a cost study at each appropriate site; (4) perform the task either by contractor or in-house under A-76 rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow this structured sequence for each candidate activity/site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost study (management study) stages
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost study consists of four stages: detailed preparation of the performance work statement/statement of work (SOW); cost estimation of government performance; solicitation of bids from commercial contractors; selection of the lowest bid after cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cost study is the most complex phase and must describe procedures for achieving efficient in-house performance and allow an equitable government-to-contractor comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Work (SOW) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The SOW should establish the government's actual minimum requirements, be sufficiently comprehensive, clear, concise and unambiguous; describe duties, tasks, responsibilities, frequencies; describe what work is to be done without prescribing how; standards are the same regardless of performer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A well-drafted SOW directly impacts solicitation, cost comparison, and performance; compliance is judged (by random sampling) and noncompliance may lead to automatic deductions ('deducts').

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance plan requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A quality assurance plan is required along with the SOW to set surveillance requirements and procedures for government quality assurance evaluators; quality standards should be objectively measurable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality control is the contractor's responsibility; the plan establishes mechanisms for administering service contracts and for applying 'deducts' for nonperformance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most Efficient Organization (MEO) basis for government estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: The DOD Authorization Act of 1981 requires that government in-house estimates be based on the 'most efficient and cost effective organization for performance' (MEO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities must use the MEO as the basis for the government estimate in cost comparisons even if MEO is not yet achieved operationally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government cost estimation components and audit
rubrics_metrics.description: Government cost estimation must calculate material, personnel, and overhead costs with standard formulas for retirement, insurance, workmen's compensation, and other benefits; the estimate must be reviewed by a qualified activity (usually an independent audit agency such as the Naval Audit Service).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The audit should also review and approve the proposed SOW and the MEO; the audit must start 120 days prior to bid opening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation and preferred contract type
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract bids are solicited after the in-house estimate is approved; firm fixed-price contracts are the preferred method, although other pricing arrangements may be approved in rare instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sealed bids are opened on the appointed date and contracting officer determines the lowest acceptable price among responsive and qualified bidders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost comparison threshold (90% rule / >10% savings)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the lowest contract price is less than 90 percent of the government cost (i.e., yields more than 10% savings versus in-house personnel-related cost), a pre-award survey is conducted and a contract may be awarded; if all contract bids exceed 90% of in-house cost, government performance is considered lowest bid and conversion does not occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 10% differential accounts for potential loss of production, temporary decreases in efficiency/effectiveness, and other unpredictable risks from contracting out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustments in cost comparison (conversion, capital, overhead, tax)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjustments include adding a cost of capital charge when government assets are required to ensure contractor performance; adding conversion costs to reflect one-time switching costs; adding additional overhead absorption when capacity is reduced; deducting potential federal income tax revenue that would be paid by the contractor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these adjustments to produce an equitable comparison between in-house and contract costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-award survey capability check
rubrics_metrics.description: If lowest contract price appears sufficiently less costly, a pre-award survey is conducted to determine if the lowest bidder is capable of performing the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A favorable pre-award survey is required before contract award and subsequent in-house dismantling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision announcement, public availability, and appeal timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: After approval, the cost study results are announced and detailed analysis made available to the public. Appeals must be lodged within 5 working days (extendable up to 15 days for complex decisions); if no appeal or discrepancies, contracting officer will award or cancel solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure public disclosure and respect short appeal windows; contracting actions proceed quickly once appeal period lapses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation timeline for in-house winner (MEO implementation)
rubrics_metrics.description: If government performance is selected, implementation of the MEO must be initiated within 30 days and completed within one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan and staff to meet the one-year MEO implementation requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: A-76 exclusions and waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories excluded from A-76 include: major system acquisitions governed by OMB Circular A-109; contractor support services (consulting, studies, professional/management support); activities performed outside the U.S.; products/services obtained from other federal agencies when authorized by law; in times of declared war or military mobilization; and DOD procurement of RDT&E (research, development, tests, evaluation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm an activity is not excluded before proceeding with A-76 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: SOW: Minimum Acceptable Quality Level (AQL) and deducts
rubrics_metrics.description: The SOW should establish the minimum acceptable quality level (AQL); when AQL is specified, contractor assumes full legal liability for meeting it; noncompliance results in financial penalties known as 'deducts'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When specific procedures are required by the SOW, the government bears some risk if compliance still results in unacceptable performance; structure deducts and AQL carefully to align incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP) principles
rubrics_metrics.description: QASPs must be fair and reasonable, equitable in application (not dependent on perceived contractor 'quality'), and similar to the Quality Control plan used by MSC for vessels retained in-house; QASPs include requirements for interaction with contractor QC plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement QASPs consistently across Area Commands and ensure they reflect the level of scrutiny MSC is willing to withstand for its own operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preventive maintenance surveillance sampling
rubrics_metrics.description: Each piece of equipment is an element of the lot for sampling; elements will be inspected, test-operated, and history cards reviewed; evaluator ratings should reflect a composite of these, noting general condition and appraising contractor performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsatisfactory ratings will be somewhat subjective but should allow shipboard managers to prioritize maintenance while maintaining general plant condition without being penalized unfairly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor repairs surveillance and quarterly sampling
rubrics_metrics.description: For three quarters each year, a list of minor repairs will be compiled from a joint walk-through by the QASP evaluator and contractor representative; performance of these repairs will be rated via random sampling during quarterly inspections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the remaining quarter (pre-overhaul), compile a detailed list and change sampling to a 100% checklist; required repairs must be performed prior to overhaul completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence of inspection detail
rubrics_metrics.description: The detail of inspection used to compile QASP lists must be similar to that presently used in inspecting MSC-operated ships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QASP and contractor QC expectations should be comparable to in-house inspection norms to ensure equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metrics for assessing A-76 effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended and used evaluation metrics include cost savings, manning reductions, ship operational readiness (e.g., time at sea), maintenance quality (including deferred maintenance), and contract administration overhead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a mix of quantitative (cost, time at sea, manning numbers) and qualitative (interviews, maintenance quality assessments) data; research suggests short-term cost reductions from manning cuts but maintenance/long-run effects may be inconclusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fallback when no bids
rubrics_metrics.description: If no contractors bid, work goes directly to the government; if no government bid, a contractor is selected to perform the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for both contingencies when soliciting bids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor pricing freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractors are free to use whatever method they prefer to calculate overhead, wages, fringe benefits, profit, and other budget items in preparing bids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government in-house estimates must be robust (MEO-based) to allow a fair comparison despite differing contractor costing methodologies.
